chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

key_terms.اسْتَأْثَرَ: to adopt partiality, to monopolize, to favor oneself or a specific group
key_terms.مَلَكَ: to possess, to have power or authority

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between holding authority and showing partiality according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this aphorism from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) succinctly captures the psychological and political tendency of authority to breed partiality (*istithar*), a concept deeply explored in Shia political ethics as the natural inclination of rulers to favor their inner circle. This saying serves as a critical warning for leaders to guard against the corruption of justice by power, emphasizing that authority often distorts impartiality unless consciously checked by spiritual discipline.
